quests.instruction: Choose the introduction that gives context and a clear position.
quests.prompt: Topic: paid internships.
options: Companies should pay interns. Some interns are paid, and some are not, depending on the company.
Many graduates take unpaid internships to gain experience, and companies offer them in many industries. Internships last from a few weeks to several months.
Many graduates take unpaid internships to gain experience, but not everyone can afford to work for free. Companies should pay all interns at least a basic wage.
In this essay, I will talk about internships and whether they should be paid or unpaid.
quests.hint: An introduction should set the scene and tell the reader what the writer argues.
quests.explanation: This introduction includes context and a position. The alternatives only describe, only assert, or announce the topic.

quests.instruction: Choose the best introduction.
quests.prompt: Topic: allowing well-behaved pets in offices.
options: In this essay, I will discuss pets in offices, looking at different views on the subject.
Offices are places where many people work every day. They have desks, meeting rooms and kitchens.
Pets are loved by millions of people around the world. Many households own a cat, a dog or a rabbit.
For many staff, the hardest part of returning to the office is leaving a pet at home. Offices should allow well-behaved pets on set days.
quests.hint: Which version connects the topic to a position?
quests.explanation: This version opens with a relatable situation and states a position. The others talk about pets or offices in general, or announce the essay.

quests.instruction: Choose the best thesis statement.
quests.prompt: Topic: a reading week at university.
options: Reading weeks exist at some universities in a few countries, and they vary in length and timing.
Reading week is a good idea for students at university, and it is one that many of them talk about.
Reading week is a topic that many students often discuss, especially near the end of each term.
Universities should schedule a reading week each term because it reduces stress and allows deeper study.
quests.hint: A thesis takes a position and previews reasons.
quests.explanation: The best thesis takes a position and gives two reasons. The others are too vague or only state facts.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is a clear, arguable thesis?
quests.prompt: Topic: phones at school lunchtime.
options: Phone-free lunchtimes would improve students' friendships and reduce afternoon distraction.
This essay is about the use of phones at lunchtime, and it looks at what schools currently allow.
Lunchtime is the break between the morning and afternoon lessons, and it usually lasts about an hour.
Many schools have rules about the use of phones, and the rules differ from one school to the next.
quests.hint: A thesis is something a reader could agree or disagree with.
quests.explanation: The correct thesis takes a position and offers two reasons. The others announce, state a fact or describe.

quests.instruction: Which thesis previews the reasons the essay will discuss?
quests.prompt: Topic: city bike hire.
options: City bike hire should be expanded because it is cheaper than owning a bike and replaces short car trips.
I believe that city bike hire is a good thing for everyone who lives in or visits a large city.
City bike hire should be expanded for many different reasons, several of which are discussed below.
City bike hire is a service that some cities offer to residents, usually through a phone app or a card.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that names the reasons.
quests.explanation: The best thesis names cost and replacing car trips. The alternatives don't preview specific reasons.

quests.instruction: Which thesis has the right scope for a short essay?
quests.prompt: Topic: student councils.
options: Schools should spend money on education for all students.
The student council bought twelve new chairs last term.
Student councils usually meet on Tuesday afternoons.
Student councils should control a small part of the school budget.
quests.hint: A good thesis is neither too broad nor a simple fact.
quests.explanation: This thesis makes a specific claim that can be argued. The alternatives are too broad or are facts.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision of the weak thesis.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Public Wi-Fi in parks is a topic.'
options: Everybody knows that Wi-Fi in parks is useful and popular, so there is no need to discuss it any further.
Cities should provide free Wi-Fi in parks so that residents without home internet can study and work outdoors.
Free Wi-Fi in parks already exists in some cities and towns, where it is used by thousands of people.
Public Wi-Fi in parks is something that people have different opinions about, depending on where they live.
quests.hint: Turn the topic into a position with a reason.
quests.explanation: This revision takes a position and names a reason. The remaining options describe or assert without support.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision of the over-broad thesis.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Technology is good for society.'
options: Schools use technology every day in lessons and in offices, and most students are used to it.
Digital tools are better than non-digital tools in most cases, so schools should use them more often.
Schools should replace paper timetables with a live app because it shows room changes immediately.
Technology helps society in many ways and should be used more in schools, hospitals and workplaces.
quests.hint: A revised thesis narrows the topic to a specific proposal.
quests.explanation: The best revision focuses on a specific change and reason. The other choices remain broad.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision of the announcement.
quests.prompt: Original: 'In this essay, I will discuss whether subscription services are worth it.'
options: Subscription services are worth it only for people who use them at least weekly.
This essay will look at subscription services from different points of view.
Subscription services are worth discussing in an essay like this one.
Subscription services are discussed below in detail and with examples.
quests.hint: Replace 'I will discuss' with the actual answer.
quests.explanation: This revision states a position with a condition. The other choices still announce the topic.

quests.instruction: Which hook leads best into a thesis about reducing plastic packaging?
quests.prompt: Choose the opening that connects to the thesis.
options: One online order recently arrived in four layers of plastic for a single pair of socks.
Packaging has been used to protect goods for thousands of years, from woven baskets to wooden crates.
Many people enjoy shopping online for clothes and other items, and the number of orders grows each year.
Plastic is a material that can be made from oil and gas, and it has been widely used since the 1950s.
quests.hint: A good hook makes the reader notice the problem the thesis addresses.
quests.explanation: This hook shows the problem of excess packaging. The others are general facts.

quests.instruction: Which hook is most appropriate for a formal essay?
quests.prompt: Topic: packaging waste.
options: OMG, have you seen how much packaging there is in the shops these days?! It is absolutely crazy!
Listen up, because packaging is destroying the whole planet, and nobody seems to be doing anything.
Packaging: some people love it, some people hate it, and it is a subject that divides opinion.
How much of your weekly shopping bill goes on packaging that you throw away?
quests.hint: Formal hooks are engaging but not slangy or dramatic.
quests.explanation: This hook asks a thoughtful question. The other choices use slang, exaggeration or a vague statement.

quests.instruction: Which hook does NOT lead naturally into the thesis?
quests.prompt: Thesis: Schools should teach basic cooking skills.
options: When I left home, I could not boil an egg.
A first-year student recently spent £40 a week on takeaways.
One in three students I surveyed could not cook a simple meal.
The first cars were built in the 1880s.
quests.hint: Which opening has no link with cooking?
quests.explanation: The history of cars has no link to cooking skills. The others lead directly to the problem the thesis addresses.

quests.instruction: Put the introduction in order: hook, context, thesis, preview.
quests.prompt: Arrange the four sentences of an introduction about water fountains at a school.
options: These stations would reduce queues, cut plastic waste and help students stay hydrated.
Our school has 900 students but only two working fountains.
On Tuesday morning, thirty students queued for a single water fountain.
The school should install refill stations on every floor.
quests.hint: The thesis comes after the context, and the preview follows the thesis.
quests.explanation: The hook grabs attention, the context explains, the thesis states the position and the preview names the reasons.

quests.instruction: Arrange the introduction.
quests.prompt: Order the sentences of an introduction about tourists and an old bridge.
options: Every year, thousands of tourists photograph the same old bridge.
Its narrow footpath, however, was built for local traffic.
A cap would protect the bridge, ease congestion and keep the experience enjoyable.
The city should limit daily visitor numbers.
quests.hint: The context creates the problem that the thesis solves.
quests.explanation: The hook introduces the scene, the context reveals a problem, the thesis proposes a solution and the preview lists benefits.

quests.instruction: Arrange the introduction.
quests.prompt: Order the sentences of an introduction about too many meetings.
options: Last month, my team spent nine hours in meetings.
Companies should set a meeting-free afternoon each week.
That is more than a full working day, and nothing was decided.
Protected time would help staff finish focused work and reduce overload.
quests.hint: Start with the specific scene and end with the benefits.
quests.explanation: The example opens, the comparison gives context, the thesis follows and the last sentence previews the reasons.

quests.instruction: Which order of body paragraphs builds a logical argument?
quests.prompt: The essay argues that a city should introduce a tourist cap.
options: Problem → cause → solution → objection answered
Cause → objection answered → solution → problem
Objection answered → solution → cause → problem
Solution → problem → objection answered → cause
quests.hint: A reader needs to understand the problem before the solution.
quests.explanation: The correct order moves from problem to cause to solution, and then deals with objections. The others start with the answer or objection before the problem is explained.

quests.instruction: Which body plan groups related points together?
quests.prompt: A writer has four points for closing a street to traffic: lower noise, cleaner air, more café income and more shop visitors.
options: Paragraph 1: lower noise and more café income. Paragraph 2: cleaner air and more shop visitors.
Paragraph 1: lower noise and cleaner air. Paragraph 2: more café income and more shop visitors.
Paragraph 1: more café income and lower noise. Paragraph 2: more shop visitors and cleaner air.
Paragraph 1: cleaner air and more shop visitors. Paragraph 2: lower noise and more café income.
quests.hint: Group points into one paragraph when they belong to the same theme.
quests.explanation: Noise and air are environmental benefits; income and visitors are economic. The correct plan groups points by theme.

quests.instruction: Which sequence builds logically, with each point leading to the next?
quests.prompt: The essay argues that schools should protect sleep with later start times.
options: Schools can protect sleep with later starts → better memory improves exam results → sleep helps students remember
Sleep helps students remember → better memory improves exam results → schools can protect sleep with later starts
Better memory improves exam results → schools can protect sleep with later starts → sleep helps students remember
Sleep helps students remember → schools can protect sleep with later starts → better memory improves exam results
quests.hint: Each idea should depend on the one before it.
quests.explanation: This sequence moves from cause to effect to action. The others place effects or actions before their causes.

quests.instruction: Choose the best sentence to begin the second body paragraph.
quests.prompt: The first paragraph explained how refill stations save money. The second will discuss the environment.
options: In conclusion, refill stations are a good idea, and the school should consider installing them soon.
Cost is an important issue for most schools, and every budget has to be carefully planned.
Refill stations already exist in some public buildings, such as libraries and leisure centres.
Beyond the savings, there is a strong environmental case for refill stations.
quests.hint: A transition points back and forward at the same time.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence links to the savings and introduces the environment. The others repeat, describe or conclude too early.

quests.instruction: Choose the best transition from the concession paragraph to the rebuttal paragraph.
quests.prompt: The concession paragraph admitted that setup costs are real.
options: Meanwhile, many people like to plan their spending carefully and to keep a record of every purchase.
These concerns are valid, but they can be managed with careful planning.
Some people have concerns about many things, and it is normal for people to worry about the future.
Planning is normally done by managers and supervisors, who have more experience of the whole project.
quests.hint: The transition should lead from admitting a concern to answering it.
quests.explanation: The best sentence acknowledges the concern and moves to the response. The alternatives change the subject.

quests.instruction: Which opening links back to the previous paragraph about quiet rooms?
quests.prompt: Previous paragraph: 'Quiet rooms help individuals to focus.' Next paragraph: about collaboration spaces.
options: Some people prefer noisy places to quiet places.
Focus alone, however, is not enough; teams also need places to talk.
Teams exist in a great many companies around the world.
Rooms can be booked online through the company website.
quests.hint: The next paragraph should build on the previous idea, not restart.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence refers back to focus and moves to teams. The other choices don't connect the two paragraphs.

quests.instruction: What should the second body paragraph do?
quests.prompt: The introduction states the thesis, and the first body paragraph develops Reason 1.
options: Present a different reason and support it with evidence.
Restate the thesis word for word.
Introduce a new topic that is unrelated to the thesis.
Repeat the first reason with only new examples.
quests.hint: Each body paragraph should add something new to the argument.
quests.explanation: A second body paragraph usually develops a new reason. Repeating, drifting or restating adds nothing.

quests.instruction: Where does the counterargument paragraph fit best?
quests.prompt: The essay has an introduction, three main reasons and a conclusion.
options: As the very first sentence of the essay
Before the thesis statement
After the main reasons and before the conclusion
After the conclusion has ended
quests.hint: The counterargument should test the argument after it has been made.
quests.explanation: After the main reasons, the writer can respond to objections. Placing it earlier or later disrupts the flow.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the best link from the last body paragraph to the conclusion?
quests.prompt: The essay argues for making a trial programme permanent.
options: There are more things that could be said about the trial, but there is no space to say them here.
That is all I wish to write on this topic, and I hope the reader has found it interesting.
Finally, the trial began in March of last year and has been running in two schools since then.
Taken together, these benefits show why the trial should become permanent.
quests.hint: A closing link gathers the argument.
quests.explanation: This sentence sums up the argument and points to the recommendation. The rest are irrelevant or end abruptly.

quests.instruction: Choose the best topic sentence for a body paragraph about teams.
quests.prompt: Thesis: Companies should offer four paid volunteering days a year because it builds skills, strengthens teams and helps communities.
options: Volunteering is a popular activity across the country, and many people take part in it every year.
Volunteering together can strengthen teams by giving colleagues a shared goal outside their usual roles.
Colleagues work in different departments of a company, and many of them rarely meet during the year.
Communities need helpers in many different ways, from cleaning parks to running food banks.
quests.hint: The topic sentence should connect to one reason in the thesis.
quests.explanation: The best sentence links volunteering to team strength. The alternatives are general facts.

quests.instruction: Which topic sentence does NOT connect to the thesis?
quests.prompt: Thesis: Local shops deserve support because they keep money in the community, offer personal service and reduce transport emissions.
options: Shorter delivery distances reduce vehicle emissions.
Money spent locally circulates among neighbours instead of leaving town.
Supermarkets have introduced self-checkouts in many towns.
Local shopkeepers know their customers and can give tailored advice.
quests.hint: Test each sentence against the three reasons.
quests.explanation: Self-checkouts are not connected to money, service or emissions. The other three each match a reason.

quests.instruction: Choose the best topic sentence for the paragraph that answers the cost objection.
quests.prompt: Thesis: Libraries should stay open late during exam periods.
options: Exam students often study alone or in small groups, and many of them prefer a quiet room to a café.
Extending hours has a cost, but the expense is small compared with the benefit to exam students.
Libraries have many different costs throughout the year, including heating, staff and new books.
Costs are numbers that are usually written in pounds, and they can be compared from one year to the next.
quests.hint: The topic sentence should signal the objection and the reply.
quests.explanation: This sentence acknowledges the cost and moves to the benefit. The others are general or unrelated.

quests.instruction: Put the essay skeleton in order: thesis, reason 1, reason 2, conclusion.
quests.prompt: Arrange this essay skeleton about students helping to set the timetable.
options: Second, shared decisions build responsibility.
Schools should give students a voice in setting the timetable.
First, students know when they concentrate best.
Overall, a student voice would improve both learning and trust.
quests.hint: The thesis comes first and the overall sentence comes last.
quests.explanation: The thesis opens, 'first' and 'second' introduce the reasons and 'overall' introduces the conclusion.

quests.instruction: Choose the best introduction.
quests.prompt: Topic: subsidised school trips abroad.
options: A week abroad can change how a student sees the world, yet many families cannot afford the cost. Schools should offer subsidised trips so that every student has the same chance.
A week abroad can change how a student sees the world. Many students enjoy travelling to different countries with their friends.
In this essay, I will discuss school trips abroad and the different opinions about them.
Schools should offer subsidised trips. Many schools have trips that go to different places.
quests.hint: Look for context and a clear position.
quests.explanation: The best introduction states the context and the position. The alternatives miss the position or announce.

quests.instruction: Which thesis is strongest?
quests.prompt: Topic: a yearly reading challenge.
options: Schools should run a reading challenge for lots of reasons, and this essay will describe several of them.
A yearly reading challenge is a topic that teachers often discuss when they plan the school calendar.
Schools should run a yearly reading challenge because it builds vocabulary and gives students shared topics to talk about.
Reading challenges are held in some schools, and they usually run for a term with a small prize for finishing.
quests.hint: Choose the thesis that takes a position and gives reasons.
quests.explanation: The best thesis makes a claim and names two reasons. The others state a fact or a topic.
